mappings.note: What grows on one plant -- the poem's opening fact, found by close reading. Rejected LO-24, which is the skim-for-usefulness outcome.
Whose love the butterflies are drunk on -- a specific point in the verse. Rejected LO-22: no idea is being weighed.
Identifies the referent of 'doosra' in a quoted line -- close examination for a specific point. Rejected CG-HIN3: pronoun reference, not poetic craft.
Whom the flower gives its nectar to. Rejected LO-24: bare detail.
Which word carries the sense of 'badappan' -- discriminating shades of meaning between santosh, ahankaar, pratishodh, dvesh. Rejected LO-25: lexical, not a search in the text.
Distinguishes the near-homophones 'meh' and 'megh' -- exactly the fine grain of vocabulary. Rejected LO-25: nothing is located in the poem.
What shines on both at night. Rejected CG-HIN3: a stated fact, not the image's effect.
Which lack cancels the merit of high birth -- the poet's central claim, to be grasped and reported. Rejected LO-25: no line states it as a fact to find.
Where flower and thorn are born. Rejected LO-22: the shared origin is stated, its significance asked elsewhere.
What falls equally on both. Rejected LO-24: bare detail.
The thorn's nature as the poem describes it. Rejected CG-HIN3: description, not appreciation of craft.
What the flower gives the bee. Rejected LO-22: located detail.
What the poet says the flower spreads in society -- the poet's idea about it. Rejected LO-25: 'in society' takes it past what any line states literally.

Asks what the thorn is a SYMBOL of -- how a poem works through pratik. Cited at goal level because no outcome among the 16 covers poetic symbol: LO-26 is folk song and tale specifically, and LO-28 concerns the learner's own use of words. NOTE: the option and key print 'drishti pravriti', evidently a corruption of 'dusht pravritti'.
Without what the poet holds lineage worthless -- his thesis. Rejected LO-25: an argued claim, not a found detail.
Where the flower is honoured (on the gods' heads) -- located in the verse. Rejected LO-22, which I keep for the item asking why.
Blank is 'dhang' -- an ordinary word, so the item is verse recall. Rejected LO-28, kept for blanks whose missing word is archaic or figurative.
Blank is 'chaandni' -- plain vocabulary. Rejected LO-28 for want of lexical difficulty.
Blank is 'bhaunr', the metrically clipped poetic form of bhaunra -- the item turns on the poem's diction. Rejected LO-25: knowing the line is not enough without the form.
Blank is 'sur' in its archaic sense of deity, not of musical note. Rejected LO-25: the demand is lexical.
Blank is the compound 'var basan' -- both words are literary ('var' = fine, 'basan' = garment). Rejected LO-25 on the same ground.
Blank is 'bedh', a literary verb stem. Rejected LO-25: word knowledge, not plot.
Blank is 'janam' -- only a metrical spelling of a common word, so this is verse recall. Rejected LO-28: nothing new lexically.
Blank is 'kali' inside the idiom 'ji ki kali khilaana' -- the set figurative phrase is the difficulty. Rejected LO-25: idiom, not detail.
How the butterflies are described ('pyaar mein doobi'). Rejected CG-HIN3: quoting the epithet, not appraising it.
When the moon shines on them. Rejected LO-24: bare detail.
Who opens 'ji ki kali' -- the agent, located in the verse. Rejected LO-28, which I used where the idiom itself is the blank.
Who takes the butterflies in its lap. Rejected LO-22: located detail.
What adorns a god's head. Rejected LO-22, kept for the item asking why.
Who nurtures both -- the one plant. Rejected LO-22: the fact, not its moral force.
How the rain falls on both (equally). Rejected LO-22: stated detail.
How the winds blow on both. Rejected LO-22: stated detail.
Who pierces the bee's dark body. Rejected LO-28: 'bedh' is glossed in its own blank item.
Who is an eyesore to all. Rejected LO-22: the line says it outright.
Who nurtures both, in short-answer form. Rejected LO-22: the equality of nurture is the premise, argued elsewhere.
The contrast of natures, assembled from the poem's own descriptions. Rejected LO-22: no claim of the poet's is under discussion.
The three specific harms the thorn does -- a close-reading list. Rejected LO-21: narrated harm, not an issue for the learner to react to.
How the flower treats butterflies and bees -- located behaviour. Rejected LO-22: no idea to weigh.

Which sort of people the poet depicts THROUGH the thorn -- grasping the idea the poet conveys by the figure. Rejected CG-HIN3, which I keep for the item that names the symbol as such; here the demand is the poet's message.
When lineage becomes worthless in the poet's view. Rejected LO-25: an argued position.
Which the poet rates higher, birth or merit -- his thesis stated as a choice. Rejected LO-20: the item asks what the POET holds, not the learner's own reasoning on caste and birth.
When, on what, and how the moon casts its light -- three located details. Rejected LO-24: no gist.
The specific harms of the thorn's hardness. Rejected LO-22: located detail.
Why the thorn irks everyone -- the poem attributes it to its hardness. Rejected LO-22: the reason is stated.
What the flower's gentleness accomplishes -- stated in the poem. Rejected LO-22: no inference required.
WHY the flower adorns the gods' heads -- the key gives 'because of its qualities', which is the poem's merit-over-birth thesis. Rejected LO-25, used for the bare 'where' version of this item.
What makes a person great -- the poet's proposition. Rejected LO-25: no line answers it directly.

The SOCIAL lesson the poet means the flower-and-thorn figure to teach -- the text's usefulness, which the key states as deeds over birth. Rejected LO-22, which I keep for items asking what the poet thinks rather than what the poem is for.
Which people the poet points at through the thorn -- his idea behind the figure. Rejected CG-HIN3: the symbol is not being named, its referent is being explained.
How the poet presents the flower's qualities -- reading his portrayal. Rejected CG-HIN3: the key answers with qualities, not with poetic devices.
